newsitem.title: USA: U.S. envoy returning to Bosnia.
newsitem.headline: U.S. envoy returning to Bosnia.

text.p: U.S. envoy Robert Gelbard will return to Bosnia on Sunday for another diplomatic effort aimed at securing compliance with the Dayton peace accords, the State Department said on Tuesday.
"He will be discussing follow through on the steps that were taken last week" during a mission on which Gelbard was accompanied by Richard Holbrooke, spokesman James Rubin said.

This includes plans for a common Bosnia currency coupon, refugee returns and work that Croatian President Franjo Tudjman and Bosnian President Alija Izetbegovic have done on improving commerce between their countries, he said.
Rubin gave no details on Gelbard's itinerary except to say he would meet "relevant leaders", or on how long he planned to stay in the Balkans.
U.S. officials said there are no plans for Holbrooke, architect of the 1995 Dayton accords that ended the Bosnia war, to return to the region.

Holbrooke left government in 1996 to become a New York investment banker but has been called back for special assignments several times. Two months ago he was named the new special envoy to try and resolve the long-standing Cyprus problem.

Gelbard, a career diplomat, is the permanent U.S. envoy on Bosnia, named recently to intensify U.S. efforts to ensure that the Bosnia peace process succeeds before NATO-led peacekeeping troops are due to be withdrawn in June 1998.
Holbrooke had lunch on Tuesday with Secretary of State Madeleine Albright, but Rubin did not provide any details of that conversaiton.
